claims: an SSE/browser projection disconnect does not stop daemon-owned work
a timer suspension is re-armed after daemon restart
signal delivery is rejected out of order and for a wrong subscription
an exact signal retry replays its durable delivery receipt
a conflicting delivery payload is rejected
objective create replay and conflict survive a daemon restart
signal expiry is persisted and emitted once
signal cancellation uses the objective control reducer and persists terminal state
accepted-but-unproven native startup becomes interrupted instead of being retried
a queued follow-up is recovered and delivered exactly once to a retained session
attention resolution is idempotent and conflicting replay is rejected
artifact publication and checkpoint commit replay by request key
artifact evidence and aggregate events remain fenced by one event cursor

known_gaps: The fixture cannot prove that a real provider accepted an unknown native request; that boundary requires provider-specific crash injection.
A process SIGKILL is not safe inside Vitest, so daemon.close() is used at explicit command boundaries and exercises the same SQLite recovery path.
Cross-machine SQLite locking and browser multi-window reconnect are outside this local acceptance gate.
